headline: Pori Moni gets bail after surrendering in assault case
summary: The actress allegedly snatched a journalist's phone and verbally abused reporters as she left the Dhaka Chief Judicial Magistrate Court.
details: Actress Pori Moni surrendered to the Dhaka Chief Judicial Magistrate Court on Thursday and was granted bail on a Tk 500 bond.
The appearance triggered chaotic scenes, with Pori Moni allegedly snatching the mobile phone of a Samakal multimedia reporter and verbally abusing journalists.
A court visitor, Sujan Chandra Moni Das, sustained a head injury and was seen bleeding after being pushed by the actress's security guards.
The actress was surrounded by approximately 11 security guards in black and others in civilian clothes who restricted the movement of people around her.
The case was filed by businessman Nasir Uddin Mahmud on July 6, 2022, involving allegations of assault, vandalism, and intimidation.
A PBI report submitted on March 18, 2023, substantiated the allegations of assault and intimidation against Pori Moni and Junaid Bogdadi Jimmy.
caption:
Pori Moni secures bail on a Tk 500 bond, but her court appearance ends in chaos and allegations of assault on journalists.

Actress Pori Moni surrendered to the Dhaka Chief Judicial Magistrate Court on Thursday and was granted bail on a Tk 500 bond.

The appearance triggered chaotic scenes, with Pori Moni allegedly snatching the mobile phone of a Samakal multimedia reporter and verbally abusing journalists.

A court visitor, Sujan Chandra Moni Das, sustained a head injury and was seen bleeding after being pushed by the actress's security guards.

The actress was surrounded by approximately 11 security guards in black and others in civilian clothes who restricted the movement of people around her.

The case was filed by businessman Nasir Uddin Mahmud on July 6, 2022, involving allegations of assault, vandalism, and intimidation.

A PBI report submitted on March 18, 2023, substantiated the allegations of assault and intimidation against Pori Moni and Junaid Bogdadi Jimmy.

headline: 53 red cards: Brazil match sets world record after massive brawl
summary: An under-20s state championship semifinal in Minas Gerais descended into chaos, shattering the previous record of 36 red cards.
details: A football match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais saw a record 53 red cards issued after a massive brawl broke out between players and staff.

The incident occurred during a state championship semifinal between Uberlandia and Mamore. The trouble began in the second half when Uberlandia officials invaded the pitch after a player was sent off.
The match was halted for 40 minutes before restarting. Mamore eventually scored in stoppage time to take a 3-1 lead, but celebrations sparked another brawl.
Referee Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto dismissed a total of 43 players, 8 coaching staff members, and 2 board members from Uberlandia.
The referee eventually declared the match ended due to turmoil and lack of security. He also filed a police report regarding threats made against him and vandalism of the dressing room.
This event surpasses the previous Guinness World Record of 36 red cards, which was set during a 2011 match in Argentina.
In a gesture of fair play, Uberlandia forfeited the second leg of the semifinal because Mamore did not have enough eligible players left to field a team.
This forfeit allowed Mamore to qualify for the final of the tournament.
caption:
53 red cards in a single match! A Brazilian football game just shattered the world record after a massive brawl.

A football match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais saw a record 53 red cards issued after a massive brawl broke out between players and staff.

The incident occurred during a state championship semifinal between Uberlandia and Mamore. The trouble began in the second half when Uberlandia officials invaded the pitch after a player was sent off.

The match was halted for 40 minutes before restarting. Mamore eventually scored in stoppage time to take a 3-1 lead, but celebrations sparked another brawl.

Referee Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto dismissed a total of 43 players, 8 coaching staff members, and 2 board members from Uberlandia.

The referee eventually declared the match ended due to turmoil and lack of security. He also filed a police report regarding threats made against him and vandalism of the dressing room.

This event surpasses the previous Guinness World Record of 36 red cards, which was set during a 2011 match in Argentina.

In a gesture of fair play, Uberlandia forfeited the second leg of the semifinal because Mamore did not have enough eligible players left to field a team.

This forfeit allowed Mamore to qualify for the final of the tournament.
